findings.title: getForLogin cache ignores organization-level invalidations
findings.body: The login cache is keyed only by realm and FetchMode and getForLogin only checks isInvalid(cacheKey). Unlike getByOrganization (which also checks isInvalid(orgId)), it never checks whether the requested organizationId has been invalidated. Organization-side changes that register an invalidation for the organization id (organization update/removal and broker association changes performed through the organization provider rather than through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.create/update/remove) therefore do not evict the cached realm+mode IdentityProviderListQuery. The cached ID set keeps being served until an unrelated IdP mutation invalidates the login key, so brokers can remain visible for an organization they no longer belong to, or remain missing after being linked, on login pages.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate can NPE on identity providers with a null config map
findings.body: The new predicate unconditionally calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) for every org-linked identity provider. IdentityProviderModel allows the config to be set to null (e.g. models built/imported from representations without config), so evaluating this predicate during the new create/update/remove invalidation in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider will throw NullPointerException and fail the whole IdP operation, whereas the previous predicate only inspected enabled/linkOnly/hideOnLogin. The config access needs a null guard (treat missing config as not public).

findings.title: Cached getForLogin loses the delegate's result ordering
findings.body: On a cache hit the method collects the cached internal IDs into a HashSet and returns identityProviders.stream(), so the order of the returned stream is hash iteration order of UUID strings instead of the order produced by the JPA delegate (which getAllStream returns in its deterministic query order). Any caller of getForLogin that does not explicitly re-sort (the login bean does, but the storage provider contract gives no sorting guarantee to other callers) will now see identity providers in a different, unstable order than before this caching was added.

findings.title: Test cleanup removes a literal "alias" provider instead of the created providers
findings.body: Both cleanup registrations in testCacheIDPForLogin use testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") rather than the alias of the provider just created ("idp-alias-" + i, and similarly at line 425). The cleanup therefore targets a non-existent provider and the 20+ identity providers created by the test are left behind in the shared test realm, making the test suite order-dependent and potentially polluting other cache/count assertions; the cleanup should capture the per-iteration alias.
